html:
The honest answer to "how much does a cleaner charge to clean a house" in Startex is that no honest company can name a number without seeing the house. A two-bedroom with one bathroom and a four-bedroom with three can differ by hours of work, and the price follows the hours. Below is how that works, so you can read any quote you get, ours included.

What sets the price of house cleaning

Every house cleaning service in Startex comes down to the same question: how long will it take a trained person to bring this home to a good standard, and how many people does it need? Five things drive that answer.

FactorWhy it matters
Home size and layoutMore rooms and square feet take more time
Bedrooms and bathroomsBathrooms are the most time-intensive rooms
FrequencyWeekly and biweekly visits cost less per visit than monthly
Pets and kidsExtra hair and traffic add a little time
First visitThe first clean is usually deeper, to reach the maintenance standard

How much does house cleaning cost in Startex?

We do not post a price list, and we will explain why. A list would have to assume an average home, and almost nobody lives in the average home. Startex is a historic mill village near the Duncan and Lyman area, which means you can find older houses with smaller rooms, original trim and long hallways right next to newer builds. Trim and layout change the work, so the same square footage can take different time.

What we do instead is simple. Perfect Services gives prices only after a free in-home estimate. A team member comes to the house, looks at the rooms, asks what matters to you and gives a firm number with no commitment. Book it by calling (864) 399-5168, texting (864) 666-8520, or filling in the form on the Startex booking page.

It also helps to know what a walkthrough looks like. We start at the front door and go room by room: how many bathrooms, what kind of floors, whether there are stairs, how many pets, and which surfaces need special care such as older painted trim. We ask what you want to see changed first, because a family that cares most about the kitchen and bathrooms needs a different plan than one that wants the whole house touched up. The visit is short and relaxed, and you do not need to tidy up for it.

Why the first visit is different from the second

People are often surprised that the first clean takes longer than the ones after it. A first visit usually has to reach the maintenance standard: baseboards and door frames that nobody has wiped in a while, cabinet handles, the track of a sliding door, the corners of the shower. After that, those spots are touched up on a rotation, and each regular visit stays shorter. That is also the reason recurring service costs less per visit than a one-time clean. We are maintaining, not rescuing.

A word on comparing quotes. If one company gives you a number over the phone without asking about bathrooms or pets, ask what it assumes. A low price built on a guess usually turns into a shorter clean or a surprise later. The point of a free in-home estimate is that the number you hear is the number for your house, and the team knows exactly what it is walking into on the first day.

Ways to keep the estimate lower without cutting corners

  • Choose weekly or biweekly visits if the budget allows, because shorter, regular visits cost less per visit.
  • Pick up toys, laundry and papers before the team arrives, since clutter-free floors and counters clean faster.
  • Tell us which rooms matter most, so time goes where you see it every day.
  • Skip extras you will not use. A first visit does not need every add-on.
  • Be honest about pets. Hair on upholstery and stairs adds time, and it is better to plan for it.

Frequency deserves its own sentence. Weekly visits keep a home at a steady level, so each one is mostly dusting, bathrooms and floors. Biweekly works for many families, though the second week can show more build-up. Monthly visits are possible, but each one starts to look more like a first visit again, which is why per-visit pricing rises as the gap grows.

What is included in a standard visit

Each visit covers kitchen counters, sink and stovetop cleaned and sanitized, appliance fronts and handles wiped, bathrooms including toilet, shower, tub, mirrors and chrome, and floors vacuumed and mopped by hand. Surfaces, shelves and furniture are dusted, beds are made and trash is emptied. Baseboards and door frames get touched up on a rotation, and light switches and other high-touch spots are wiped. If you want the inside of the oven or refrigerator, that is closer to a deep cleaning visit and is priced separately at the estimate.

How long it takes and when we can start

For an average home the visit runs a few hours with a small team, and the first visit tends to be longer. Startex is about 7 miles east of Greer, around a 15-minute drive on US-29, so scheduling an estimate in the same week is usually realistic. Ask when you call and we will tell you what is open.

Not sure about the format? Read how another Upstate team approached it in house cleaning before selling a home in Greer, or look at house cleaning in Lyman if a neighbor of yours is nearby. When you are ready, send the free estimate request and we will set the visit.

The short version: the price is the time, the time is the house, and the only way to know the house is to look at it. That is why the visit is free.
